role: The second reading: each entry read to refute it, not to admire it.
method: Each fragment read whole beside what show.cjs prints for the grape (GRAPES, GRAPES_PLUS, TASTE, INTRO_GRAPES, GRID_SAY, GRID_READS, the service rows) and beside the Codex's region readings and banks where they name the grape.

Every fact that the Codex's reviewed records do not already state was put to search, at most five searches a grape: parentage, home, synonyms, the appellation rules, the service figures, the climate claims behind the Old World and New World lines.
The glass read as a blind taster would: each note asked whether a taster would nod, and each prose field scanned for a family word in disguise.

The four lines counted and said aloud for the five beats in order; the sale read for its two sentences; the cards and questions read for one key, four options of one kind and nothing given away; the compare tells read from both sides against the other fragments that name these grapes.
node .scripts/grapes/build-grapes.cjs --lint --chunk g1 run after every round of edits until it printed six of six sound. The writing build was never run.
limits: This session reached search alone: no source address could be opened, the national institute's and the ministry's hosts among them. A rule is cited as search results quoted it.
The lint note on lees in the Melon de Bourgogne forty five second line was read and left: the same breath says the spent yeast.

Parentage of Cabernet Sauvignon and the year the work was published (1997); the name from the French for wild; Fumé Blanc as a California name of the 1960s; Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé on facing banks.

changed.was: the upper Loire is cooler, on limestone and flint
changed.now: Marlborough's bright sun, long days and cool nights build intense aroma and hold the acidity; the upper Loire, far inland on limestone and flint, gives quieter fruit.
changed.why: A false cause. Sancerre is semi continental, more than 480 kilometres from the sea, with short, hot summers; Marlborough is a cool, sunny, maritime region. The Court's grid calls both cool. Nothing read says the upper Loire is the cooler of the two.

sources.title: New Zealand Wine: Marlborough regional guide

changed.was: Marlborough's Awatere Valley and Martinborough make leaner, stonier wines, and a warm year or riper picking can give Sancerre a hint of passion fruit
changed.now: Marlborough's cooler, windier Awatere Valley makes leaner, greener wines, and a warm year gives Sancerre riper, rounder fruit; barrels appear on both sides.
changed.why: Martinborough's style stood on no source. The regional body calls the Awatere cooler, drier and windier, and tasters find it leaner and more herbaceous. Reports of the warm 2018 and 2020 harvests in Sancerre speak of riper fruit, more flesh and pineapple, not of passion fruit.

changed.now: richer old bush vine wines, often fermented and aged in barrel
changed.why: Picked riper stood on no source, and many old vine growers pick for freshness. The barrel is now often, not a rule.

changed.now: more body and often vanilla from barrels lean South Africa
changed.why: A call a flight would break: much old vine Chenin Blanc is raised in old wood and shows no vanilla. The riper fruit and the body are the tell; the vanilla is frequent, not constant.

changed.why: Decades for a dry wine found no source in this session, and TASTE.age keeps decades for the sweet wines.

changed.was: the one grape of Muscadet; made from Melon de Bourgogne alone
changed.now: the grape of Muscadet; made from Melon de Bourgogne
changed.why: The rule of the plain Muscadet appellation now names Melon as the main grape and Chardonnay as an accessory one, at no more than 10 per cent of a holding's plantings. Sèvre et Maine, Coteaux de la Loire and Côtes de Grandlieu are still Melon alone.

tested: Grown in Burgundy since the seventeenth century (the national institute's sheet says the first traces date from then); the regional name since 31 July 1937; Bouzeron the one village name, by a decree of 17 February 1998.
Where it is planted; the golden strain of Bouzeron and its thin skins; Chardonnay and Pinot Noir in Crémant de Bourgogne; the grape in Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova, Ukraine and Russia.

changed.was: often on the higher slopes; Burgundy's higher slopes in most years
changed.now: often at the top and the foot of the slopes; Burgundy's hilltops and Hautes Côtes in most years
changed.why: Half the truth. The grape is relegated to the highest and the lowest ground, the land Chardonnay and Pinot Noir leave it; only in Bouzeron is it said to hold the upper slopes.

changed.was: under a splash of blackcurrant liqueur in a Kir
changed.now: poured over blackcurrant liqueur as a Kir
changed.why: The Codex's own service reference builds a Kir cassis first, the wine poured over it.

changed.was: One village, Bouzeron, is given over to it, and grows a golden strain whose thin skins turn gold as they ripen.
changed.now: One village name, Bouzeron, is kept for it alone, and its golden strain has thin skins that turn gold as they ripen.
changed.why: The name is kept for Aligoté; the village is not. The appellation covers two communes, which also grow Chardonnay and Pinot Noir under other names.

changed.was: Bouzeron's sheltered slopes, and warm years across Burgundy
changed.now: Bouzeron's marl slopes, and warm years across Burgundy
changed.why: Shelter stood on no source; the white marl of Bouzeron's slopes does.

open: The thin skins of the golden strain stand on a merchant's magazine and on the regional body's page as the author read it; no primary text was opened.

changed.now: acacia blossom; lemon zest

Grapefruit and lime point to Sauvignon Blanc and Riesling and no source gives them; the Austrian study gives pear, apple, walnut and a hint of acacia flower, and notes for Alto Adige give lemon zest. Hay is the mark of Silvaner in that grape's tell against this one.

codexRecords: js/regions/france.json, the Loire reading: Melon de Bourgogne is called Muscadet's only grape. True of Sèvre et Maine, Coteaux de la Loire and Côtes de Grandlieu; the plain Muscadet appellation now admits Chardonnay as an accessory grape.
js/data-intro.js, question i-r0p7056l: its explanation says Melon has been the sole grape of Muscadet ever since 1709. The same rule loosens it.
js/data-regions.js, question r-rkgv0zwg, and the Burgundy reading: Bouzeron is dated 1997; the decree is dated 17 February 1998. The author's flag, confirmed.
TASTE.world for Chenin Blanc reads old while the plan fixes contrast. No fault in either: the flag says where the grape is from, the plan what a guest meets on a list.
